summary: READ-ONLY visual/observational QA pass across Apollo Home/Guard at 4 viewport sizes (360x740, 412x915, 390x844, 810x1080) plus Apollo state exploration (resting, sniffing, barking reached; ears_up, growling, biting NOT reachable via suggested inputs in this mock build) and Guard capability status matrix (Active/Permission required/Coming later/Unsupported). NO CODE WAS MODIFIED — git diff remains empty (only an untracked yarn.lock). Findings categorized below as (a) concrete layout/accessibility issues or (b) subjective/business-logic observations, per the human's report-first instruction.

ui_bugs.issue: (b) Subjective/content mismatch, not a layout bug: during the transient 'sniffing' window (right after tapping Verify now), the GIF/animation correctly switches to the sniffing pose (state variable includes sniffing prop), but the title/meaning/reason text (lines 115-116, using resolution.state directly, not the local `state` var) still shows the PREVIOUS state's copy ('Apollo is patrolling'). Screenshot: hero_sniffing_immediate.png shows sniffing-pose GIF next to 'Apollo is patrolling' text — a brief visual/text mismatch during every Verify-now tap.

(b) No cropping or excessive whitespace found for the 170px GIF in its circular ring at any of the 4 viewports (360/390/412/810px width) — dog fills the ring proportionally, ring/glow visible but restrained (colour wash confined to the circular ring area, not full-card), consistent across resting, sniffing, and barking states checked.

integration_issues.flow: Check-a-link classifier vs suggested test fixtures
integration_issues.issue: (b) Business-logic observation, not a redesign bug: pasting https://www.commbank.com.au/netbank on /check returned 'Nothing found' (resting/patrolling tone), not the expected ears_up state. Pasting https://service-mail.top/verify returned 'Apollo is barking' (barking tone, high confidence, listed as known phishing) instead of the expected growling tier. The classifier appears stronger/coarser than the gate1.test.ts fixtures implied for this build — flagging for main agent's awareness since ears_up and growling states could not be visually verified in this pass.

integration_issues.flow: dev-tools PROTECTION_UNAVAILABLE adapter scenario -> Verify now -> Home hero
integration_issues.issue: (b) Pre-existing observation (also flagged in prior iteration_46 report): selecting the PROTECTION_UNAVAILABLE chip in /dev-tools and then tapping Verify now on Home did NOT change the hero state to 'visibility lost' / 'Apollo can't see right now' — title stayed 'Apollo is patrolling' and the visibility pill stayed 'Limited visibility' rather than 'No visibility'. Could not visually verify the 'visibility lost' hero appearance in this pass.

integration_issues.flow: Barking -> Biting via block action (mock adapter)
integration_issues.issue: (b) Expected mock-build limitation, not a bug: producing a barking event (commbank-netbank-secure.xyz) then tapping 'Block this destination' (event-block-button) on the Patrol detail returns 'Block could not be verified. Apollo is still barking.' The mock SecurityAdapter cannot verify a block, so the Biting state (verified_block=true) is architecturally unreachable in this web/mock preview — confirmed by on-screen copy 'Mock adapter (demo): nothing is blocked on this device.' Biting hero state could not be visually verified.

action_items: Decide whether ears_up/growling tiers are reachable at all in the current mock classifier, or if the gate1.test.ts fixtures referenced in the task need different concrete inputs for this build — could not visually QA these 2 of 6 states.

Decide whether dev-tools adapter scenario chips (e.g. PROTECTION_UNAVAILABLE) are meant to feed into resolution.state/visibilityLost via Verify now, or are cosmetic-only in this build (same open question raised in iteration_46).

Optional/cosmetic: ApolloHero title/meaning/reason (lines 115-116) currently read resolution.state even while the sniffing GIF plays — consider whether copy should also softly reflect 'checking...' during the transient window, or leave as-is (intentional per code comments: 'Apollo is actively re-checking' is meant to be a GIF-only cue). No action required unless the human wants text unified with the animation.
critical_code_review_comments: Confirmed no cropping/whitespace issues with the 170px GIF (HERO_SIZE) inside its 156-192px ring/glow across 360/390/412/810px viewport widths, for resting, sniffing and barking states.

Confirmed no text truncation/overflow/awkward wrapping on hero title/meaning/reason, tile labels (4 primary + 6 'All checks' tiles), Guard capability card bodies, or Check-a-link result cards (including the long barking 4-bullet reason list) at 390px width.

Confirmed Protection/Verification cards stack column at 390/412/360px and sit side-by-side (flex:1 row) at 810px via the WIDE_BREAKPOINT=700 useWindowDimensions check in home.tsx — visually verified, no gap/overlap issues.

Confirmed Guard capability chevron logic: chevron (ChevronRight) renders ONLY on the actionable 'Permission required' row (site_guard); Active rows (link_guard, known_threats, connection_guard, message_guard, app_guard), 'Coming later' (share_intake), and 'Unsupported here' (site_guard after switching PROTECTION_UNAVAILABLE) all correctly show NO chevron.

Card spacing (spacing.xl=24px content padding, spacing.md=12px between capCard items), tile minHeight=84px, and tileIcon 36x36px all read as comfortably >=44pt tappable in screenshots — no sub-44px targets observed on tiles, buttons, toggle, or tab bar icons at any of the 4 widths.

Text/icon contrast against #F5F7FA/white/surfaceTertiary looked adequate in all screenshots — no borderline/illegible text found on DevTag 'MOCK' badges, inactive nav icons (grey #52606D on white nav), or secondary body text (#52606D on white/surfaceTertiary).
Bottom nav bar (white background, amber #F4B942 active icon+label, grey inactive) renders with consistent height/icon-label spacing across 360/390/412/810px widths — no visual imbalance noted.

Safe-area top/bottom spacing (insets.top + spacing.md header padding, standard ScrollView bottom padding) looked correctly applied in all phone-size screenshots — no header text clipped under a notch area or content hidden behind the nav bar in this web-preview rendering (note: web preview cannot fully simulate a physical notch/home-indicator, so this should be re-verified on a real device/Expo Go build).

success_rate.backend: n/a - not tested per request (frontend-only, read-only visual pass)
success_rate.frontend: 4/4 viewport x Home/Guard screenshot pairs captured cleanly with no layout bugs found; 3/6 Apollo states visually confirmed clean (resting, sniffing, barking) — 3/6 states (ears_up, growling, biting) could not be produced via the suggested test inputs in this build and are reported as open observations, not confirmed bugs

seed_data_creation: None — used existing mock adapter/classifier. Produced one transient barking Patrol event (commbank-netbank-secure.xyz check) and attempted (unsuccessful) block action; no persistent code or data changes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Onboarding flow from a cold load: tap the first 'Continue' text button on the welcome/state-explainer screen, then [data-testid='disclosure-accept-button'] on privacy disclosure; poll for [data-testid='apollo-hero'] up to 45s (completeSetup() network calls vary 5-40s). IMPORTANT: each mcp_browser_automation tool invocation does a fresh page.goto/reload of page_url, which resets all React state back to onboarding — do ALL steps for a given test flow (viewport changes, tab navigation, state production) inside a SINGLE script call; do not assume state persists between tool calls. /check, /email etc. are full-screen modal routes without the bottom tab bar, so tab-* testIDs are unavailable there — use page.go_back() or page.goto('.../(tabs)/home') to return. Ears_up and growling states were not producible with the suggested URLs (commbank.com.au/netbank -> resting; service-mail.top/verify -> barking, not growling) — a next tester should explore stateMachine.ts / gate1.test.ts more directly, or ask main agent for confirmed working example inputs per tier. Biting is not reachable in the mock/web preview because the mock SecurityAdapter always returns 'Block could not be verified.'
rca_of_issue: No code bugs were found needing RCA — all layout/accessibility checks (GIF sizing, text wrapping, spacing, touch targets, contrast, responsive breakpoint) passed cleanly. The 3 unreached states (ears_up, growling, biting) are either (1) a classifier-tuning/business-logic question (which URL patterns map to which tier) or (2) an architectural mock-adapter limitation (block verification), both explicitly out of scope for this read-only pass and left for the main agent/human to decide on.
